ratings.note: Forced-colours capture (probes/6) shows the Status column blank, so the float fault is gone for those users (impact 3, static so p 2). Few users meet it: the bay tablet is an iPad running Safari, which has no forced-colours mode (f 0). s=4; I rate 3 because the affected group is small on the declared platforms.

aria.yml shows only the table, with no help or link. Two of five sensors are amber or red in the shipped data (f 2). An untrained volunteer cannot tell what to do and must find the lead (i 2). Partly learned once the lead explains it (p 1). s=3.

768 audit screenshot shows status given by dot hue only, with no text. Colour-blind volunteers are on every rota and check several times per shift (f 2). They cannot see the Reservoir float fault, which blocks top task 3 (i 3). Learning does not help (p 2). s=4.

aria.yml shows Conductivity vs EC probe, Acidity vs pH probe, and so on, on every visit (f 3). Novices have to map the names themselves (i 1), but once learned the mapping sticks (p 1). s=3; I rate 2 because after a shift or two it is an annoyance more than a recurring difficulty.

Cards show only a verdict and never a range. 'Warm' on 23.7 °C leaves open whether action is needed, on top task 2 every check (f 3, i 1). The checklist helps once learned, but the meaning of 'Warm' still recurs (p 1). s=3.

In probes/4, after-reload.png shows the switch back on and the status 'automatic' after it was set to manual. This happens on every reload or second viewer of the shared tablet during the critical reservoir journey (f 2). The setting may not hold, so the pumps can dose into an empty tank (i 3). Users cannot learn around it (p 2). s=4.

In probes/7, after-toggle-back shows that one tap restores automatic with no prompt. Accidental taps are rare (f 0), even with wet gloves on a shared tablet, but when one happens dosing restarts into a drained tank (i 3). It recurs, but care reduces it (p 1). s=3.

768 screenshot shows the chart with time labels only, and the range exists only in the alt text. It is seen every view (f 3) and persists (p 2). Impact is small (i 1) because the current pH card already says 'In range'. s=3; I rate 2 because the overnight trend is secondary to the current verdict for top task 2.

In aria.yml the Status cells are empty for all five rows. The declared screen-reader volunteer cannot find out which sensor needs attention (i 3, blocks task 3). Few users are affected (f 1), but learning cannot help (p 2). s=4.

forced-colors-manual.png shows no switch drawn, only the label, though the status sentence remains. Users of forced colours are rare on the iPad and phone platforms (f 0). They would struggle to find the control for the critical task (i 2), and this happens on every visit (p 2). s=3.

The manual-state inventory shows no pump-start control, while the text says 'when you start them'. It is met on every reservoir change (f 2). The volunteer has to ask or look at the controller (i 1), and learns it once (p 1). s=2.

768 screenshot shows a green 'Topped up 09:30' card next to a red Reservoir float dot, with nothing linking them. This is present whenever the float faults (f 2). It may lead a volunteer to trust the tank before reservoir work (i 2). It persists until the fault clears (p 1). s=3.
